utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go through the usual preliminaries and the extraordinary preliminary that I would expect one thing after the other. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. Mr. Brdjanin, can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Please take your seat. Appearances for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Anna Richterova, assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you both. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, David Cunningham. Today I'm assisted by Aleksandar Vujic and we are legally authorised by the American Government to go forward. So we are here in a representative capacity for the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am pleased to hear that, Mr. Cunningham, and I am sure that Mr. Brdjanin is even more pleased than we are. I thank you and good morning to you both. So preliminary number 1. The motion that you filed the day before yesterday, Mr. Cunningham - when I say "you," it's Mr. Ackerman - for these proceedings to be adjourned, do I take it that the substance of that motion is now moot?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: It is moot, Judge. We are ready to go forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So, Registrar, please take note of that. That motion does not need to be decided any longer. It's being declared moot. Number 2, before we can proceed with this witness, Mr. Cunningham, we need to hand down a decision on the protective measures that were asked for him by the Prosecution. What is being asked with regard to this witness, who is BT97 -- correct me if I am wrong, Madam Richterova, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes you are right. It's BT97.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The request is that he testifies with a pseudonym and distortion of image and voice. Is that acceptable to you, Mr. Ackerman -- Mr. Cunningham?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, we do not have any objection to the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: While we are at it, let's deal with the next witness, BT94. What is being asked is only facial distortion, Madam Richterova, can you or Ms. Gustin.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Facial distortion, no?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Facial distortion and pseudonym. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And pseudonym. Is that agreeable?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have no objection to that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So both motions are being granted and this is being decided orally for the time being. The decision, the written decision, will be handed down during the break. There are some changes that need to be made that I notice here. So good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it that you can hear what I am saying in a language that you can understand, in other words, that you are receiving proper interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. So we can proceed. You're here to give evidence, I'm sure you know that, and you're going to give evidence in the trial which has been instituted against Radoslav Brdjanin. Before you do so, you are required by our rules to make a solemn declaration equivalent to an oath that in the course of your testimony, you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text is contained in a document which the usher, Madam Usher, is going to hand to you now. What I ask you to do is to stand up, take that text in your hand, read it out loud and that will be your undertaking with this Tribunal that as stated you will be speaking the truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, you have to turn off your mike.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Please take a chair. I suppose you are following what I was saying before. When I mentioned "BT97," that's you. You are not going to be referred to by your name here but only by a number, by a pseudonym, and that's in order to protect your identity, as requested by you. In addition, you have asked for voice and face distortion and we have also granted those protective measures. If, usher, please, could you assist the witness? If you look at your monitor in front of you, on the video mode, and the -- you will see how others are going to see you. Something moving behind a lot of squares, cubes, that's you. But that's how others are going to see you. And that's visual distortion. Any person following these proceedings also will not be able to hear your own voice. They will hear another voice and that's what we call voice distortion and that's again to protect your identity, so that you can put your mind at rest that your testimony will be heard by others but there is nothing that should give away your identity. Having said this, I need to give you some advice, because sometimes who messes it up and creates problems is the witness himself. In the course of the testimony you will be asked questions, and there may be a time when, by answering that question, you need to give information about yourself which would identify you. For example, if I ask you which street did you live in and in which town? Obviously, if you answer that question, everyone -- it will be easy for many people to identify you as today's witness. So we will take all precautions ourselves and I can assure you that both Madam Richterova and Mr. Cunningham will be doing their utmost to ask me to go into private session when these questions are being put and answered so that when we are in private session, no one can follow the proceedings. In open session, they can hear what you are saying through someone else's voice, but in private session no one knows what you are saying. So then you are at liberty to give the information because no one will know it, except the people inside this room. But we all have a right to know that. If we are not in private session, take care not to say anything that may reveal your identity. That's all I ask you. Having said that, I think the last thing I need to tell you is that you will first be asked a series of questions by Madam Richterova; and secondly, you will then be

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it, Ms. -- Madam Richterova, that you are tendering the witness's statement in evidence as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I can do it -- I can do it in due course because I think it's important that we hear everything but it depends whether we will be able to go through all these things with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because I thought we had agreed yesterday that it will be admitted under Rule 92 bis and then --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it will be, but we have to wait for the translation. And it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Go ahead. Go ahead. Madam -- he's all yours. You may start questioning him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to show you a piece of paper on which you will see your name and please state whether yes or not it is your name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P2122 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 2122 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we go to private session for a little while?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. We will go into private session now, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, first I would like you to direct your attention to the events which happened on 11th of June, 1992, and events which followed that date. Did you observe anything unusual happening in the town on 11th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I noticed that lamps in the street were on across the River Vrbanja, and in the morning I saw anti-tank metal mines in front of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How many of these anti-tank mines did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Four of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What was your reaction? Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I went to where my inhabitants were and they sent me as a reserve police force member to report this to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you go to the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, I did go to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you observe anything unusual on your way to the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. I noticed armed soldiers in camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Apart from these armed soldiers, did you observe that someone would be maltreated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. In front of the building where Ilija lived [redacted] [redacted], I noticed a large group of soldiers who were already beating Ilija [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After seeing this maltreatment, did you go to police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. I did later. I was passing by.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Whom did you meet in the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: At the entrance, or rather outside the police, I noticed armed soldiers, two or three armoured vehicles. There was a soldier with a radio station on his back standing at the entrance to the police station. He was on his way out. Inside I met Jovan, an active service police officer, I didn't know his last name, and Anto Pranjic who was the commander of that police unit. Neither of them were carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You mentioned that you saw armed soldiers in front of the police station. Can you describe these soldiers. Did you first -- first, did you know them maybe by sight and second, what did they wear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Those I knew were from Territorial Defence. They were not wearing any weapons at that moment and those who were carrying weapons, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you describe the uniforms which they wore?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms, green and black.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did they wear any hat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. They were wearing hard hats or helmets, red.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We heard "red." What was red on these hats or --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Red berets.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You also mentioned Anto Pranjic. Can you tell us what was his ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: He was a Catholic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And those soldiers and members of TO, did you know what ethnicity they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Serbs, orthodox.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you report that you saw anti-tank mines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. I did report that to Jovan and to Anto Pranjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what was their reaction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: They looked surprised. They couldn't believe what I was telling them. Jovan was the duty officer and he said that he needed to go over to the TO to check what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you return back to the bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, I did, accompanied by Anto Pranjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did Anto see as well these mines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He saw them too.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After you returned to the bridge, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Anto left me there to watch the mines until he called some people over who could actually remove those mines.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How long did you stay at the bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I stayed for about 20 minutes, then I had to go back after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I went towards the centre of Kotor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what was happening there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I told my neighbours there that mines had been noticed and that we didn't know what to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you also inform them about the soldiers you saw in the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What was decided? What did you do after this -- after you told them what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: The decision was for the women and children to go to the woods, and it was decided that we would at some point follow them to provide security for the group.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you have any weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. I got it from the reserve police unit. It was a semi-automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The other men who gathered at that point, did they have some weapons as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: They did, about 18 pistols but most of the weapons were actually hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you follow the women to the woods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the woods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: About seven days.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: During this stay, during the time you stayed in the woods, were there any negotiations between your people in the woods and some Kotor Varos representatives?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us something more about these negotiations? Who was on your side? Who did -- I will repeat my question. Who represented --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly, who represented your side.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Who represented your side and who represented the other side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Our side was represented by Sadik Fific, Matos Matosevik, Sakib Debic, and Huso Huseinovic. The other side was represented by Savo Tepic and Slobodan Dubocanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What did you learn about these negotiations? What was the result of these negotiations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: They told us to lay down our weapons and be loyal citizens of Republika Srpska. They said that I, as a reserve police officer, should go back to my job as reserve police officer. They said that if I refused to go back, I would be made to hand my weapon over.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you surrender your weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What about the other men who had weapons? Did they surrender their weapons as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. They did too.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know whether your houses were searched?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Were they searched in your presence or when you were in the woods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: While we were still in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What were you are told about these searches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: They said that everything had been searched through and that everything was okay, that we need not have any fear and that we could go back to our homes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And as you stated, you returned to your houses after seven days spent in the woods; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After you returned to your houses, were there some other contacts with Serb soldiers and I am referring to the time after you returned to your houses and the date 25th of June.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us when it was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: The same day we returned to our homes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: They sent over messengers, Serb soldiers, who were going from house to house telling us to assemble at a junction where the railway line was crossing the road leading to the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Who did you meet at the crossroad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I met Slobodan Dubocanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you know Slobodan Dubocanin from before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No, not from before. He just said his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you know where he was from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: He did say himself that he was from Kotor Varos but that he didn't live there. He said he resided in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Who else was present at the crossroad? Only Dubocanin or were there some other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: There were other people there too. Zoran Tesic, outside Nedjo Djukic's house pointing a rifle at us, and there were a number of other soldiers standing by and around us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you describe for us these other soldiers. What did they wear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: All of them were wearing camouflage uniforms and weapons, automatic and semi-automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did they wear any hats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. Helmets, different kinds of hats.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did Dubocanin ever mention to you the name of his unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No, he didn't. But we called them specials because they wore those caps.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What do you understand under the word "specialist"? What was their task or what did you know about them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Well, what they told us themselves, that they were better, better prepared and better trained than other units and soldiers. Probably they had a headquarters somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did Dubocanin tell you anything during this gathering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. He separated the men from the women and children, and once he had had the men counted, we were about 85, he said that the group was never to grow or to diminish. He said that we would be safe and free to go back to our homes. He said our lives were more valuable than houses or buildings. He said that we should try to keep several families together in just one house, if it proved possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After this meeting with Dubocanin, did anything else happen? Was there any shooting, any searches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Units were deployed at checkpoints manned by Serb soldiers providing security for the citizens of Kotor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Now I would like to direct your attention to the events of 25th of June. Can you tell us what happened on 25th of June in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: In the morning, soldiers rounded us up and took us to Luka Marcinkovic's house first.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned "soldiers rounded us up." Who were these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Those were Serbs, Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And where was he and the others that were rounded up?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, you heard the Judge's question. Where was you at the moment when the soldiers entered the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I was in my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And these soldiers, did they come to your houses and order you to gather at one point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They simply drove us out of the houses. I didn't even have time to tie up my shoe laces and I had to keep my hands behind my neck.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You mentioned Serb soldiers. Were they the same soldiers which were present when Dubocanin met you or were they different soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: They were both the same soldiers but new, different soldiers were there too. I knew one of them personally. I didn't know his name but I knew that he came from Grabovice.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You said that you were in your house. Who else was taken from your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I was taken, my father, my brother, my brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did -- your mother was present at the time when you were taken out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. And they brought them later.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand. You said, "and they brought them later." Whom did you mean "they"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: My mother, my wife, my brother's wife, my sister and the children.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did your mother ask where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know what was the reply?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: He said, I could blow their brains out on the spot if you ask this again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You said that you were taken to one place, to a house of -- can you please repeat the name of the person of -- who was the owner of that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Luka Marcinkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How long did you stay in this house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Until they rounded up all the citizens of Kotor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Were there -- in this house, were there only men or also women with children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Only men.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many approximately how many men were there in this house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: At that time, about 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After that, where were you taken? Or did you stay in the house or were you taken somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Dusko Vujicic arrived; Dragan Bojic was with him. We were lined up outside the house in rows of four and then we were taken outside Rasim Tatar's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, did you know Dusko Vujicic and Dragan Bojic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Who was Dusko Vujicic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: He was an active service police officer at the Kotor Varos police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: At the time when he round you up -- out, did he wear any uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. Blue and green, camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Who was Dragan Bojic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: He was the secretary of the Rad company.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And did this person wear any uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, blue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Richterova. Is Dusko Vujicic still alive to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware of his whereabouts? Where does he live? In which town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say for sure, but I believe he's still in Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what he's doing in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps he's retired now. Police officers usually retire earlier than other people. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Richterova, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, when you were accompanied or escorted by these two men, were you ordered to give them anything from your possession?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. We had to hand over our personal documents, wallets, watches, belts, shoe laces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Were you accompanied only by these two men or were there some other soldiers or policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: There were many other soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: We were taken -- while we were standing outside Rasim's house, we handed over all of our belongings and then four of us were singled out from the group, they said that a Serb had been killed and that we should confess who it was that had killed the Serb. They said that each time a Serb was killed, they should kill five of us in retaliation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You were in the group of these four?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Richterova, if you intend to ask the witness to mention the names of the components of this group, we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's go into private session, please, for a while.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You said that you were asked who killed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Okay. Go ahead now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You were asked who killed the Serb. Were there some other questions? Did they maltreat you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Not at that time. They brought the others into Rasim Tatar's house. They brought us inside too but at that moment we were a separate group. Mujo Zeher was singled out and then when he came back he was crying and his clothes had been torn to pieces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Rasim Tatar's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: We stayed for about an hour. It took maybe not a long time but I think we stayed there for about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was the age range of people who were kept together with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: There were people aged 15 and the other end of the range was people aged about 60.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: At this stage, was anyone released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. Tatar, Eno, who was underage; Kemo Zeher; and Goran Terzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, after one hour spending in this house, where were you taken then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: We were then taken to Stipe Zebic's house -- Stipo Zeba's house in the direction of the village of Ravne.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How many of you were in the column?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: At that point, there were about 85 of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Where in the house or in the property of Stipo Zeba were you taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: At first, they left us between the garage and the house itself and we had to keep our heads down and our hands above our heads. They beat us there and mistreated us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: These soldiers, did they wear red berets as well as you described before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. There were some among them wearing red berets but some were not wearing red berets.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Those who didn't wear red berets, what type of hats did they wear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: They wore helmets, some even wore nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were beaten while in front of the house. Did you know whether any women or children were present in the house or in the surrounding area of this house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. There were some women in the garage with children.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I don't know. They were in the garage and we were in front and to the side of the garage.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: While you were in front of the Stipo Zeba's house, was anyone separated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. Since they kept asking who killed the Serb and no one responded, they said we should raise our heads. They even asked for volunteers, they asked for someone to kill. No one responded and we were ordered to raise our heads.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After you raised your heads, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: They singled out five persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Esad Muminovic, Seval Djuvelek, Samir Avdic, Mevludin Vilic. As his wife had just had a baby, his father asked that Mevludin should remain, that he would take her [as interpreted] place and then he said that he should be the fifth person.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of his father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Resid Vilic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Where were these people taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: At the railway station, the street in front of us, they were taken across the railway tracks behind this transport vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After they were taken behind this transport vehicle, did you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. We heard an order being given, a burst of fire, and we heard someone saying that they should be sure not to miss.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you see anyone of these men at some later stage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Resid Vilic at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Was he alive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No, he was dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us after these -- after these -- after five people were taken away, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: We were lined up, two by two, we were ordered to move along the railway line in the direction of the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: On the way to the town, was anyone maltreated? Was anyone killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we go to private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, while you were in leaving the property of Stipo, did you -- were you able to observe what was happening with the houses in Kotor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. The houses were already on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know who set the houses on fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: They singled out some neighbours from Kotor, Serbian soldiers accompanied them, the soldiers were told that nothing should remain, that they shouldn't leave any stables untouched or any stores untouched and that they shouldn't approach the houses, that they shouldn't come close to the houses, because they might be booby trapped.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: These neighbours who were separated, were they of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. They were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And these men were ordered to set the houses on fire; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. They were given the orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Then you already described how you went towards the bridge and this transporter accompanied you. Can you tell us more what happened on the way towards the town? Did you know where you were taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: They took us in the direction of the hospital. We got to the crossroads, in the direction of the hospital, and they returned us to the hospital again, which is where they took us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can I show the witness a map? It's Kotor Varos town map. It has not been tendered into evidence yet so I would like to tender it into evidence under P2123. If we could place it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And please show us where you were taken from and show us the way you were -- you had to undergo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Here we were gathered in Luka Marcinkovic's house. We headed towards the railway track. We were taken to Rasim Tatar's house, and from his house we were taken to Stipo Zeba's house, in the direction of Ravni, that's about here. We were then returned again over the Vrbanja bridge in the direction of the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, can I stop you for a moment? You mentioned a minute ago that something happened to Idriz Fific. Can you one more repeat what happened to him and where it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: It was more or less here. He was leaning against a fence because he was no longer able to move. He was leaning against a fence of a plot of his own, and later I heard that this is the spot at which he was killed. I personally saw him when he was leaning against the fence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know what preceded to the fact that Idriz Fific was leaning against the pillar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. For the record, the witness has pointed to the lower part of the box opposite photos 2 and 3 on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Before Idriz Fific died or was wounded, what happened? Was there any shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. There was shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Who was shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Serbian soldiers who were by our sides opened fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you please proceed with the map and show how -- show us how you continue and what else happened before you reach prison -- hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: When we got to the main street in Kotor Varos, we headed towards the hospital. We got to the crossroads. Then we were taken back to the sawmill, roughly speaking to -- as far as the new police station, and then we were taken back to the hospital and taken on to the grounds of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm done with this map. Sir, you mentioned that on the way to hospital, someone was thrown to the water. Can you please describe how this incident happened and who was thrown to the water.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There you are. You've made the first mistake of the day, because now by mentioning his name everyone will be able to identify you. So let's redact this part, please? And we go into private session and we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness a few photographs. They are -- the first one is P2320.16.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what we can see on this picture and what happened here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: This is the hospital building. We were moving in this direction from the gate. We were taken to this building, to the pavement in front of the building of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What did you see in front of this building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: They lined us up here and then we had to crouch two by two, we had to keep our heads bent, we had to place them between our legs. It was very difficult to see anything. We could only see when we stood up, when we had to do something. At the entrance behind the fence, they had a dog, an Alsatian, who was tied up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When were you in front of this building, were you maltreated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you please describe what happened to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: They beat us and they walked over us, they would hit us with their rifles, they would ask us what our names were, they called us Ustashas, balijas.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know who was in command of these people who were beating you or did you see any men who might be in command of these men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I noticed Dragan Bojic; Dusko Vujicic; Dusko Maksimovic; Rajko Skoric; Dusko Krejic, a soldier whose nickname was Mama; and many others.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what Dusko Vujicic did when you saw him in front of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: In front of the hospital, and I'm almost 100 per cent certain, he was sitting on a chair. He called out the names of citizens of Kotor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You said he called out a name of a person. Did he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's not what he said. He said he called out the names in the plural, in other words, of citizens of Kotor. And you're suggesting that he merely called out the name of a person, which is different.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I didn't have transcript in front of me, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You said he called names of people. Did he call them off top of his head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I apologise. He called out the name of one person, not of several persons. He was a -- looking at a list.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Tell us what was the name of this person who called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Should I say the name?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, you can say the name of the person who was called by Dusko Vujicic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Miralem Avdic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Tell us what happened to Miralem Avdic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: He asked him whether he had been at the foundation of the SDA assembly in Sarajevo and said, "You are the person." 1 (Redacted) 2 (Redacted) 3 (Redacted) 4 (Redacted) 5 (Redacted) 6 (Redacted) 7 (Redacted) 8 (Redacted) 9 (Redacted) 10 (Redacted) 11 (Redacted) 12 (Redacted) 13 (Redacted) 14 (Redacted) 15 (Redacted) 16 (Redacted) 17 (Redacted) 18 (Redacted) 19 (Redacted) 20 (Redacted) 21 (Redacted) 22 (Redacted) 23 (Redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On second thoughts, Madam Richterova, going through the next paragraph in his statement, I think he -- we better redact a part of what his -- one of his previous answers consisted of. Madam Registrar, could you please print me out the last 30 lines, more or less, of his testimony, and I suggest we go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's break now for 25 minutes, please. We will resume at five to 11 and we will continue in open session, as far as we can. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, we finished before the break that you and other men took Miralem Avdic towards the pile of other bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can I show the witness now the Exhibit P2320.18.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what we can see on this picture.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Here we can see the hospital compound, the football pitch, this is the hospital fence, there is a village here behind the hospital. In front you can see the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Tell us what happened at this place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Around about here, they gave orders to dig a hole, a grave in which to put the citizens of Kotor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you still remember who was present at that place? And I'm talking about the soldiers who took you to the hospital. Did you recognise any one of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Rajko Skoric, Dusko Maksimovic. And then outside the hospital, I saw Dragan Bojic, Dusko Krejic. There was another soldier nicknamed Mama.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Were all these soldiers present when you were digging the hole?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The soldiers were there. I didn't do any digging but there were several other people who were ordered to dig. I can't remember who they were but I heard later that Mujo had been killed near the fence, Mujo Zeher.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: At this point, did anybody else was -- did anybody else was killed or maltreated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us who he was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Myself, Ivica Matijevic, Enez Terzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened to Ivica Matijevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: When we were singled out from the group, separated from the group, I saw that he had been bitten in his cheek by a dog.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we show the witness Exhibit P2320.17.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what we can see at this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: This building is across the way from the building where we were first made to crouch. That's the other side. And then towards the gate, the entrance to the hospital, there is another large building where a dental clinic. This is an apple tree. Here is where logs were piled up. Over there was a pile of bodies, people who had been killed. This is the gynaecologist's building for women. Also within the hospital complex.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you see Ivica Matijevic anywhere close to this area that we can see on this picture?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop. Let's redact this last answer, please, and we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, witness, I ask you to repeat this part of your answer. You stated that Ivica was ordered to move towards the pile of dead bodies that you mentioned earlier on. Can you now repeat describing what happened next, please. And if you know who shot him, could you tell us also who shot him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was ordered to start moving towards the pile of dead bodies there. They told him that he was an Ustasha, and then commander Dragan Bojic passed in front of us. He looked at us and moved on. I saw that it was about here, near the pile of bodies, Ivica fell down on the ground and I really couldn't say which of the soldiers had fired. I later heard that he had been hanged from a tree.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, you also mentioned the name of Enez Terzic. Can you tell us what happened to Enez Terzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: He was -- a dog, a German shepherd was let loose on him. They said that it was a killer dog and that members of the HOS would have paid several thousands of German marks for the dog but that they valued the dog much more and that we shall see for ourselves how the dog goes about killing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I saw the dog knock him down to the ground and his legs had already been injured. He had scratches on his arms.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did he survive the attack of the dog?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Was there any other incident that someone would be taken away and you didn't see him later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Rajko Skoric took one man away, before they had ordered us to hand over fuel too so that they could have some reserves. However, the man who was taken away at that point never returned later.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Ivo Kljajic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, can you now describe what happened to you after all these killings happened. What happened further in front of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I feel that we ought to go into private session for a while here, Madam Richterova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I apologise that I wasn't thinking about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So let's go into private session, and you're going to be asked a few questions about yourself and we will be in private session so you can answer them without any problems at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Witness, I know that this is difficult for you. If you need a break, if you need a small, a short rest, a short break, let me know. Just tell me. I mean, we have absolutely no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I'm ready to continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, did you see any bulldozer, any truck or any big machine somewhere in the area of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. It was near the gate inside the hospital ground, outside the dental building.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you just only specify what did you see? What big machine you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: It was a digger, an excavator or a bulldozer. A soldier drove it and turned it towards us, pinning our backs against the wall of the dental building.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: When he had us pressed there, that small space, and kept pressing us against the wall, then it would back off and then the soldier told us, "I'm sorry, my brakes weren't working properly."

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Was anyone injured when you were pinning by the bulldozer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. There were people who were injured.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know in which way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I met a person in prison who had had his arm injured and another's chest was crushed or pierced by a jag of the loader.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the area of hospital? For how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: We stayed almost the whole day, started raining, and one of the soldiers said, "Look, even God's on your side. God is saving your lives." So they had us lined up and took us back -- took to us prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Cunningham, how much time do you require for your cross?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Certainly no more than an hour. I think I feel very, very confident that Ms. Richterova is almost finished, and I feel confident that we will finish with this witness today. I see no need to keep him over the weekend. I know he needs to get home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Mr. Cunningham and thank you. So, Ms. Richterova, you regulate yourself accordingly, please. I expect to you leave Mr. Cunningham an hour for his cross. I mean the last session will last three-quarters of an hour so you have roughly another three-quarters of an hour yourself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I will finish much earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, in prison, where were you taken in the prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: We were taken to the old prison near the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Were you taken into a cell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many people were together with you held in that cell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: At that time, about 45 persons. The next day, more people arrived.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You said the next day more people arrived. Did you know from which villages were these other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you tell us the names of the -- these villages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Vrbanjci and Rujevica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After they arrived, how many of men were caught in this cell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Between 80 and 85.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How big was this cell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Roughly 6 by 5 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When did you receive your first meal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: On the second day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What type of meal did you receive that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: They said this was to be our breakfast, lunch, and dinner. It was just stale bread. It was moldy. It was very hard. There was potatoes, mixed with a lot of water.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: After you ate this food, did you -- did anything happen to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. We got sick with stomach-ache. We all needed to go to the toilet very often.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you have toilets either in the cell or somewhere which you could use?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: At the other end of the corridor, to the left of the cell, we did have toilets.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Could you use the toilet any time you wanted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No. Only when they let us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: If you wanted to use toilet and they didn't allow you, what -- how did you solve this problem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Old plates that we used were used for these needs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Were there any windows in the cell in which you were kept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. There were windows which were about 120 by 60 centimetres large.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Were these windows opened or closed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Often they had to be kept closed. Then a soldier would leave them open and then another soldier would order them to be closed so that we would end up suffocating in that cell.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you have enough space for you to sleep, to lie down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: How long did you spend in prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I spent about seven days in that prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Were you interrogated during the time you were in prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Slobodan Dubocanin entered with a hat on his head.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did he interrogate you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What kind of questions did he ask you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: He wanted to know who had killed Sadik Fific. Since he was a close friend of his, he wanted to know who had killed him. He wanted to know which one of us had killed him so that he could personally deal with that person.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Dubocanin, when we are talking about this man, how did he treat you personally and how did he treat other men who were kept in prison, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: He ordered me to count the people there. I tried to do so but I wasn't successful. My right eye was closed. Later he ordered me to sing songs with the prisoners who were with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, you stated your right eye was closed. Can you elaborate on this? Why your eye was closed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Because of the blows to my head, when my head was bent, someone kicked me in the head.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did it happen in prison or when you were in hospital area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: In front of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know how Dubocanin treated other men in prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: An elderly person from Rujevica was allowed to smoke, a chair had been brought in for that person, and he was -- he said that no one should touch that person.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you witness Dubocanin or any other people, any other soldiers, beating people in prison, while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: At the entrance to the prison, I saw such things.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you elaborate on this, what such things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: At the entrance to the prison, we had to enter one by one. I saw Dusko Vujicic there, and he would kick or punch the people while they were entering. And on the right-hand side, in front of the prison, in front of a house, and on the stairs, I saw Gavro Teinovic sitting there. He was observing the people entering. Dusko Vujicic didn't beat me himself, but a policeman did beat me. I assume he was from Skender. He hit me with a pistol behind -- at the back of my neck. I fell down in the corridor. He told me to enter. I crawled in. I was crawling on all fours. There was another one there. He hit me. He told me to turn left. I entered the room on the left-hand side. I saw Goran Zaric, an active-duty policeman who was taking down the details, the personal details, of the people. He would enter us in a list. I entered, he hit me again. I entered the first room on the right. Slobodan Dubocanin entered that room on several occasions later. He ordered us to sing. He ordered me to count the people. He said that we were to blame for what had happened to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, you just described how you were beaten. Did you suffer any consequences of this beating? Did you have any medical problems while you were in hospital -- in prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. I was sitting on a bench at the entrance to the room on the left. I was quite simply incapable of moving. When I stood up, I had to lean against the wall. I had pain all over my body. I couldn't eat. They tried to get me to lie down but I was not able to lie down because of the pain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He hasn't quite read you, Madam Richterova. It's not your fault. Were you spitting blood as well? Because he --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I just intended to ask that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Because he didn't -- please go ahead. I was just trying to give a hand.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You heard the Judge's question. Please, can you tell us whether you were also spitting and urinating blood, as you describe it in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. I was spitting out blood. There was blood in my urine. It was difficult for me to urinate. I think that I still feel the consequences now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you still remember the day when you were released?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Here be careful because there is a lot of information that could identify him. So if necessary, whenever you ask me, Madam Richterova, we will go into private session. I leave it in your discretion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us when you were released.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: From the prison or?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, from prison.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I think I have provided you with a document about this. I can't remember the exact date now. But there is a document certified by Savo Tepic and it contains the date I was released and taken to a house, where I was kept under the surveillance of the Serbian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we go to private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Madam Richterova. Let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: When did you leave the municipality of Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I think I left the municipality of Kotor Varos on the 25th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you leave on convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. We left in a convoy that was supposed to be safe and we left in the direction of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you have to sign any documents before you left Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I didn't have to.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat that answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. We have some problems which would require you to repeat your answer because the interpreters in their booth couldn't catch up -- couldn't hear what you were saying, so if you could speak up a little bit and repeat your answer, please. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you turn --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. There was a document. A person put -- left his fingerprints on the document and this was valid for me too.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Do you know what -- what this document stated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: It stated that I was leaving my municipality on a voluntary basis and that I was the -- leaving my property and that for economic reasons I was forced to leave, and not because of the war or for some other reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Was it true that you were leaving voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, did you have an opportunity to read your statement which you gave to the investigator of the Office of the Prosecution on 15 and 16 August, 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Did you made yesterday any corrections of this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like this opportunity and tender into evidence the statement and the amendments which were done yesterday and it will be tendered under P2322, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It will be 2322.1, that being the statement itself. And if you are tendering also the addendum to the statement, that would be .2. Do you agree to that?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I agree to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Cunningham, do you have any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. These two documents which are brought together now are being --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I apologise. We have a declaration in accordance with Rule 92 bis, and in fact, this declaration contains both the statement and the addendum, so now I'm a little bit confused. Maybe we could still tender this document as one document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, all right, yes, yes, yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So it would be as mentioned before, P2322 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. And they are being admitted under seal with the number that Madam Richterova mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Sir, I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I concluded my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Richterova. Mr. Cunningham? Now, Witness, look at me. I need to explain something very simple but of great importance for this Trial Chamber. You are now going to be asked a series of questions by Mr. Cunningham, who is one of the lawyers defending Mr. Brdjanin. Cross-examining you as a witness is a right that this Trial Chamber acknowledges to the Defence. It's not just this Trial Chamber. It's a right acknowledged everywhere. Which basically means that if Mr. Brdjanin through his lawyer has a right to cross-examine you, to put questions to you, arising out of the various answers that you have given already and arising out of this statement that has now been tendered in evidence, you have a corresponding responsibility, obligation, under the law to answer the questions that Mr. Cunningham will put to you, the same way you have answered the questions put to you by the Prosecution. In other words, in accordance with the solemn declaration that you made earlier on today, that is, you need to answer, to say the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth when you answer the questions that are put to you. You have no right to draw a distinction, to make a distinction, you have no right to say, "yes, I am prepared to answer the questions of the Prosecution but I don't want to tell anything to the Defence lawyer." You have no right to do that. So if there are any questions that we feel you shouldn't answer, then obviously we will stop you from answering them. And the same advice and caution that I gave you before, try -- if you feel that by giving some information we need to go into private session, just draw my attention to that and we will go straight into private session. Did you follow me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thanks. Mr. Cunningham, may I ask you please to proceed with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you some questions. If you do not understand my question, will you please let me know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your microphone, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I know that you want to be out of here, and the quickest way for that to happen is for you to listen carefully to my question and to answer only the question that I ask you. Do you think you can do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask some background questions, so I think we need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session straight away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to take to you the day that you discovered what you have described as anti-tank mines on the bridge. The bridge connects -- am I correct, this is a bridge that's part of the roadway that connects Banja Luka to Vrbanjci and points beyond Vrbanjci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No. That's to the side of the road. The connecting road. The road connecting the villages of Kotor and Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: You -- that morning, I believe, you told us that you discovered the anti-tank mines and you went to the centre of town to report that. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And, Judge, because I'm going to talk about his superiors, can we go into --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into private session for a couple of questions and then we return to open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to jump ahead just a little bit and I'm going to ask you a question about when you and other individuals were hiding in the woods, and I believe you told us that you hid in the woods for about seven days. Am I correct that you hid there for seven days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And during the time that you were in the woods, did you have the opportunity to meet any of your fellow Muslims who had acquired or had firearms with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No. No. There were no such people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I thought you told us at one time in your group that, for example, you had a weapon and there were 18 pistols and a number of hunting rifles. Do you remember testifying to that this morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. But we were not the same group. We were each with our own families, and I thought you were referring to that, to us sticking together as a group, which was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: My recollection is that the people in that group turned all their weapons in to your representatives who were involved in the negotiations. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not talking about your group and the guns we just talked about. I'm talking about other Muslims, other Bosniaks, that were in the woods in the area of Kotor Varos, that had weapons. Did you come across any people who had weapons, any other Muslims who had weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I did not move about at all after I was caught; I was in prison. I was not free to move about.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And I understand that. I'm talking about the seven days that were you in the woods hiding and then the short period of time that were you allowed to stay at your house. During that time frame, did you or did you not see any other people besides your group that had weapons? And when I say "other people," I'm talking about Muslims or Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: During --

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, I need to go into closed session for a real quick question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into closed -- closed session or private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thought you had changed your policy for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. We go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I apologise again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: After your negotiators returned, they told you that you could return to your house and stay in your house. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: You decided -- and don't tell us what your job was but you decided that you were not going to go back to your job. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your homes were searched and during the search, were either you or one of your representatives present during those searches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No, not me. Representatives were there but I don't know about that, though, but I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: You had mentioned earlier in your testimony today something about houses being booby trapped. Do you remember testifying about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No. Those were just warnings, placed there by soldiers so that the houses would not be booby trapped.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to talk to you -- I want to talk to you about your arrest and the events that followed, and it is not my intention to make you relive those events, so I'm just going to ask you some very, very specific questions. Your testimony is, I believe, that you were arrested and released as indicated by the face of the document that shows your release, I believe you were released seven days later, on 1 July 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And if you need to look at the document again, please do so, but my notes indicate that the face of the document says that after reviewing the interview and the operative information, it did not indicate that misdemeanour or criminal proceedings should be instituted against you. Do you remember reading that when you looked at the document just a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I didn't read through the whole thing but I saw the date. There was a signature, a stamp. I still own the original of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to take you back now to talk about some of the events that happened after your arrest. I think you told us that after you were taken into custody, that you were marched towards the railway line, that you were -- you and the other people you were with were ordered to form four rows and then you had to hand over anything of value that you had. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: While you were standing out there in these four rows, there were repeated questions about who was responsible for killing the Serb soldier. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Shortly after this happened, the questioning while you were standing in four rows, ultimately you ended up in a shop owned by or operated by Rasim Tatar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And it was at -- while in his shop that the men who were guarding you discovered that there was a minor, Rasim's son. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Rasim's brother's son, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: But the fact is he was, I believe, 15 years of age and he was allowed to be released. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: You also told us that two other people there were allowed to be released, Zemo Keher [phoen] and Goran Terzic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Kemal Zeher, Kemal Zeher.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And believe me, I apologise for my pronunciation, but why were they released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Goran Terzic was a child from a mixed marriage, and as for Kemal, he was suffering from the consequences of some (Redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: On the hospital grounds, you told us about some things that you witnessed and some acts that were committed by Dusko Vujicic, and I want to ask you about the shootings that you just -- the incident involving Dusko?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment before you answer. I think what the witness said about the second of the two persons that you mentioned earlier, as far as Kemal is concerned, I don't think this -- what Kemal suffered from should be of -- for public consumption, so I'm ordering that that part of the -- after the words, "Of some disease," the rest be deleted, be redacted interest the transcript. In other words, the words starting from (Redacted) and ending, (Redacted) Full stop. Sorry to have butted in like this, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Absolutely no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will repeat, myself, the question to the witness.
