Witness, Mr. Cunningham just put the following question to you which I'm reading out to you and then I would kindly ask to you answer it: "On the hospital grounds, you told us about some things that you witnessed and some acts that were committed by Dusko Vujicic and I want to ask you about the shootings that you just -- the incidents involving Dusko? " If you want to elaborate on that, Mr. Cunningham, you may. Otherwise, we pass straight to the witness and to have him answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: With your permission, I'd like to clear up the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: My understanding is that you were ordered to crouch down and to have your heads -- your head placed between your knees so that you couldn't see what was going on. Have I described the position that you were forced to get into?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: How is it, then, that you could see Dusko Vujicic do the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I wasn't quite crouching that low down. I could see the lower part of his body, his legs, his hands, and the position of the pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Did it appear that anyone had given him any sort of order to shoot the pistol or was he doing it on his own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I don't know whether there was an order or whether he did it of his own free will.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'm going to take you now to the time that you spent in the prison at Kotor Varos. How many other -- were there other rooms that other people were detained in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes. There were other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And did you ever have the opportunity to look at the other rooms or see the other rooms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Every time I'd go to the toilet, sometimes I caught glimpses of open doors to other rooms and someone on their way out.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Did those open rooms, did they have windows like yours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Well, some may not have. Some may have. I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's fair enough. While you were there, did you -- there at the Kotor Varos prison, did you see any women who were detained in the prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And where were they detained at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I saw a woman who was the opposite side from our room, across the way, there may have been more, I don't know. There was a mother and her daughter. Perhaps other women were kept in a different place, but I didn't see that because I was not where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I want -- after your release, you were allowed to stay, I think you described it as a home that was being watched by the Serbs. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: In fact, it was someone's summer house. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Ultimately, you were able to make your way on to a convoy bound for Travnik and I want to talk to you about that. Did you have to pay any fee for -- to get on that convoy, to get on a bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: When you say "not me," that suggests to me that someone else had to pay the fee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I always only speak on my own behalf and on the behalf of my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: My question is this: Did someone in your family pay your fee to get into -- to get on the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No. None of my family, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, I have a question that I need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's go into private session for just one question. Thank you, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: This is my fault because I forgot to ask you this question earlier, sir. We talked earlier about the anti-tank mines by the bridge. That day, did you ever hear any of the soldiers, any of the other armed people, talking about the anti-tank mines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That day, was there any accusation that the anti-tank mines had either been laid by Croats or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And who -- I take it it was the Serb soldiers that were making that accusation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Well, they were kind of surprised, but the man who had crossed the bridge said it himself. He suspected that the Muslims and Croats had laid those mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And was that while you were -- you and the other individuals were taken into custody, were they trying to find out whether you or the people that were in your group were responsible for laying the antitank mines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's all I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Cunningham. Is there re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No, there is no re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Janu, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Judge Janu from the Czech Republic would like to put some questions to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, at the looking at the map of Kotor Varos, it's evident that Vrbanja River is dividing the town into two parts. You were giving us the ethnic composition of the Kotor, and it's -- from the numbers you gave to us, it's evident that there is a predominant population of Muslim ethnicity. Would you be so kind and clarify for the Chamber what was the ethnic composition of Varos, just roughly, which ethnicity had the majority there, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: Donji Varos, well, roughly speaking the same structure as Kotor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Thank you. And my other question, when you were asked and Mr. Cunningham touched it again, when you were asked who killed the Serb, repeatedly, who killed the Serb, I would like to know, was the name of that Serb ever mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No, no. The name was never mentioned, nor was the body ever shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: And my other question is: When Slobodan Dubocanin was trying to investigate, to find out, who killed the Sadik Fific, I think that was his name, my question is: Was there any reasonable possibility that that this person, Fific, could be killed by anybody of you? Was it possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No, no. It would not have been possible. We were together. It was more a provocation, you know, among us, who could have killed the man with us or anyone else for that matter who was not with us. It would not have been possible. We had to keep our hands behind our heads, and we were surrounded throughout this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: And my last question is: You said that there were certainly a moment in the prison that you were in very bad condition, you were spilling blood and urinating blood. My question is: Did you or somebody else from your colleagues -- from the other prisoners, ask for medical help for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: The third night, I was unconscious. Persons urinating into the pales or buckets we had were pouring urine all over me so I regained consciousness, and I found out from Besim Tatar, his wife was a Serb, she brought some pills, tranquilisers and I took some tranquilisers and that really helped me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: So you were never given any medical aid from the people who look from -- from the guards in the prison or from anybody who was for this purpose in the prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Thank you, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We've almost finished. Now only two very short questions that I would like to ask you. And this is with reference to the hospital where you were detained and the other prison of Kotor Varos where you also were detained. What I would like to know is whether there appeared to you to be any person there to be in control, in command, of these two places, when were you in the hospital? Could you identify anyone to be in command there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I assume that the commander, the commander of the police station at the time, was the commander -- was in command at the hospital. His name was Dragan Bojic. Slobodan Dubocanin was present so he was probably in command too. So I would say the two of them were perhaps in command. I couldn't say for sure but they were present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And with regard to the old prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: At the time, Zaric, Goran, was the commander of the prison. He was an active-duty policeman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you know if Slobodan Dubocanin is still alive?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, he's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know. I want to confirm what another witness stated actually. Yes. I'm waiting for your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT97
utterances.text: I said that I really don't know whether he's alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Thank you. That brings us to an end of your testimony. I apologise to the interpreters and the technicians and the rest of the staff for having stayed longer than we were supposed to, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the reason I'm here, I'm sorry, I have something urgent to raise. If Your Honour wants a break, we can raise it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How long?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It will take five minutes, I hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see what response there is from the interpreters. We have no problem in breaking and resuming because we --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then I'm quite happy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But if the interpreters can live with this and we stay for another five minutes or so? And then we --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: That's fine with the interpreters, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, Your Honour, and we needn't trouble the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. We'll dismiss the witness. Witness, I would like to thank you -- sir, look at me, I would like to thank you for having come over to give evidence in this trial and I'm thank you, not only on my own behalf but on behalf of Judge Janu and Judge Taya and also on behalf of the Tribunal. You will receive all the attention and assistance you require to enable you to return home as soon as possible according to your wishes and on behalf of everyone present here, I should like to wish you a safe journey back home. Thank you. The usher will now escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Ms. Korner, did I hear you well you want to go into private session?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
